issues.problem: The negative prefix is hyphenated here but nowhere else in the chunk (anaghaḥ 70, arogaḥ 71, avidhavāḥ 72 are written solid). Inconsistent convention.
Bracketed gloss inside the translation; rākṣasa is left untranslated and unbracketed everywhere else in the chunk (61, 66).
The verse has only taṃ 'him'; 'राक्षस' is carried over from 44 and is an addition.
There is no primary root √duḥkh; duḥkhita is the -ita participle of the denominative duḥkhaya- (or duḥkha + ita).
issues.fix: m. inst. sg., ppp denom. duḥkhaya- (duḥkha + ita)

patch.value: m. inst. sg., ppp denom. duḥkhaya- (duḥkha + ita)

issues.problem: ca is 'and'; 'but' adds a contrast the text does not mark.
uttama means 'highest, foremost, excellent'; 'huge' is an interpretation (reflected in English 'huge' and Hindi 'विशाल'). The note admits it, but the gloss should give the dictionary sense first.
'tawny as gold' is a comparison compound (upamāna-pūrvapada karmadhāraya), not a tat-puruṣa.
No demonstrative in the text (sa ca ... vānararṣabhaḥ); 'that' is added.
dhyāyantīm is 'thinking, brooding' (English 'brooding'); 'ध्यानमग्न' suggests absorbed in meditation, a different shade.
grahaṇaṃ samupāgamat = 'came to / underwent capture'. 'submitted' adds willingness, which is only stated in 61 (yadṛcchayā), not here. The Hindi passive is fine.
'भी' makes the clause concessive ('even though knowing'); the Sanskrit has plain jñātvā with no api. Unsupported addition that changes the logic; the English correctly has none.
Gloss treats it as the noun 'circumambulation' but gram gives m. acc. sg.; the noun is n. If m., it is the adjective agreeing with rāmam ('having made Rāma pradakṣiṇa'). Make gloss and gram agree.
issues.fix: n. acc. sg. (noun; or m. adj. with rāmam)

patch.value: n. acc. sg. (noun; or m. acc. sg. adj. with rāmam)

issues.problem: daivata 'deity' is neuter (daivatam); inst. pl. -aiḥ is the same but the gender label should be n.

The draft reads durbhikṣa-bhaya as a dvandva ('famine and fear'); the equally natural reading is a tat-puruṣa 'fear of famine' (free from the fear of famine). The alternative should be recorded, and the choice of past tense 'were/थे' for a verbless verse between past narration (70) and future predictions (72-76) is a decision that should be stated.

patch.text: durbhikṣa-bhaya-varjitaḥ may also be read with durbhikṣa-bhaya as a tat-puruṣa: 'free from the fear of famine'. The verse has no verb; 'were' is supplied though 72-76 are future.

issues.problem: This e-text writes avagraha as an apostrophe elsewhere (so'bhyagacchat 46, so'bhigamya 63, loke'smin 75, śūdro'pi 79), so o + a without avagraha here is more likely a missing avagraha ('rogaś) than genuine hiatus; the note states hiatus as fact.

patch.text: Since this e-text marks avagraha with an apostrophe elsewhere, 'arogaś' here may be a missing avagraha ('rogaś) rather than a true hiatus; left as printed.

issues.problem: The class-2 optative of √i is iyāt (short i); the long-vowel form īyāt is from the by-form √ī 'go, attain'. Label the root as √ī (= √i). No machine patch because the same w occurs four times in the unit.

summary: Chunk 2 (units 41-79) is a careful draft: every printed token is accounted for, sandhi is undone correctly, the three text_flags (61 unmuham>unmuktam, 71 nirāyamo>nirāmayo, 73 cāgrijaṃ>cāgnijaṃ) are real typos with correct suggestions, the two stray-mark flags in 79 are right, and medium confidence is used honestly where readings are inferred (48 śaṃsat, 61, 71, 73, 79). No invented variants; the edition's 3-line units (46, 49) are kept and no regrouping is suggested. Issues found: 1 error (61 Hindi adds a concessive 'भी' not in the text) and 17 minor: small unsupported additions in translations (45 'राक्षस', 50 'but/किन्तु' for ca, 56 'that/उस', 60 'submitted'), a bracketed gloss in English (44), a shade of meaning (58 ध्यानमग्न), one interpretive gloss (51 uttamam 'huge'), five grammar-label corrections (49 root, 54 compound type, 63 gender/function mismatch, 68 gender, 79 root), one split-convention inconsistency (41), and two notes to add in 71 (alternative compound reading and tense; probable missing avagraha). All but the 79 gram issue carry machine-applicable patches.
